extracted.intended_audience: readers of Rabelais / students and scholars of Renaissance satire and folk belief
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted passages are from a satirical Renaissance prose narrative that treats rules and sayings about dreams, omens, fasting, and consulting seers; the subtask is to capture the prescriptive or evaluative 'rules' embedded in the narrative. Useful for analysis of folk interpretive standards and comic treatment of belief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dreams ending with a start indicate present evil or future mishap
rubrics_metrics.description: “every sleep that endeth with a starting, and leaves the person irksome, grieved, and fretting, doth either signify a present evil, or otherwise presageth and portendeth a future imminent mishap.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: Hecuba and Eurydice awoke in a start and then suffered immediate disaster; Aeneas’ start awoke before a naval tempest; Turnus’ start preceded war and death. Such dreams may signify a latent internal sickness or impending external calamity; treat a startling awakening as a warning to provide remedies or prepare for misfortune.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformations in dreams are metaphorical signs of real-world fate
rubrics_metrics.description: Dream metamorphoses are to be read metaphorically rather than literally (e.g., not actually transformed into a tabor or chough but corresponding events will occur).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: becoming a tabor (drum) means one will be soundly beaten; being changed into a chough implies theft (the dreamer will be robbed, especially at night). Interpret dream-transfigurations as symbolic analogues of physical or social events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Horns in dreams commonly symbolize cuckoldry (but can have alternate meanings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional interpreters (Artemidorus, Virgilian lots) read horns as indicating cuckoldry; Panurge contests this, offering alternative readings (horn of abundance, satyr-horns as signs of fecundity or mythological attributes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard interpretation: horns = cuckold. Alternative/contextual readings: horns may be the Amalthaean horn (cornucopia) implying abundance; mythological figures (Diana, Bacchus, Jupiter Ammon) bear horns without indicating infidelity. Use context, comparison with authorities, and cultural imagery to choose interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mood-trajectory of an apparition distinguishes divine from demonic
rubrics_metrics.description: Cabalists distinguish true (favourable) and false (perdition) apparitions by their emotional arc: a favourable angel terrifies at first but ultimately brings consolation and leaves the seer joyful; the angel of perdition initially cheers but ultimately abandons the person troubled and angry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge apparitions by their ending state: if the vision concludes in comfort and sustained joy, it is likely favourable; if it leaves the seer perplexed or distressed, suspect a malign source.

rubrics_metrics.name: If sleep (a gift) ends in wrath it portends misfortune
rubrics_metrics.description: If repose and rest (considered a heavenly gift) terminate in anger or indignation, they portend unlucky fate or proceed from infernal rather than divine sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat peaceful, restorative sleep as auspicious; disturbed sleep that ends in wrath should be read as omen of disaster or a sign of malicious influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excessive fasting and lack of food distort mood and dreams—avoid skipping supper
rubrics_metrics.description: Panurge confesses fasting too long made him wake angry and vexed; not to sup at all is condemned as offensive to Nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical rule: maintain regular meals to preserve temperament and avoid ill dreams or irascibility. Historical/monastic practices (fast to noon) are discussed but excessive abstinence is ridiculed when it harms well-being.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monastic culinary timing: earlier matins -> sharper appetite; longer boiling -> better beef
rubrics_metrics.description: The sooner monks rose (for more lessons), the sharper their appetite; the longer beef was on the fire the better and more tender it became — the aim being nourishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practical folk guideline about food preparation and appetite: long, slow boiling improves tenderness and digestibility; rising early increases appetite so food is valued and thoroughly prepared. This is offered to explain monastic rituals around meal timing and cooking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heed counsel regardless of social outward appearance
rubrics_metrics.description: Through the Alexander anecdote the text advises not to despise lowly persons with useful counsel: 'What could it have cost him to hearken... ?' — ears exist to hear, so listen even to humble advisers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open-mindedness toward advice: do not dismiss a messenger because of shabby appearance; valuable knowledge may come from unlikely sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of women's folk wisdom in prognostication
rubrics_metrics.description: Panurge praises old wives and women as 'sage' and 'presage' women, asserting their counsels are often as authoritative as legal rubrics and historically honoured (e.g., ancient Germans prized old women’s responses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat female folk practitioners and 'old wives' as competent sources of practical knowledge and prognostication rather than dismissing them on gendered grounds; cultural precedent supports giving weight to their counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consulting a sibyl/seer requires offerings and ritual readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Panurge brings food, drink, money, and a gold ring as gifts; the sibyl performs ritual acts (turning spindles, casting coins in shells, burning laurel and heather) before producing verses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical expectations when seeking a seer: bring appropriate offerings; be prepared for symbolic ritual procedures and cryptic outputs (verses, signs) rather than straightforward answers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguous prophecies require careful contextual interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: The octastich produced by the sibyl is cryptic and open to divergent readings (Pantagruel reads disgrace and cuckoldry; Panurge attempts a positive spin).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept terse prophetic lines at face value; consider wider context, compare with other divinatory sources (dreams, lots), and be prepared for multiple plausible meanings—prophecies often demand interpretation rather than literal acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: It is common to foresee others' misfortune but rare to foresee one's own
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘It is a very ordinary and common thing amongst men to conceive, foresee, know, and presage the misfortune... of another; but to have the understanding, providence, knowledge, and prediction of a man's own mishap is very scarce and rare.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A skeptical note on the limits of divination: expect that prognostication tends to be outward-focused and that self-knowledge of impending personal calamity is uncommon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of classical exempla as justification for interpreting dreams and omens
rubrics_metrics.description: The narrator repeatedly appeals to classical stories (Aeneas, Hecuba, Eurydice, Turnus) and authorities (Artemidorus, Virgilian lots, Fabius Pictor) to validate rules of dream interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When construing omens or building an interpretive rule, marshal precedents and authoritative examples; cultural and literary exempla serve as evidence for interpretive claims in folk or learned frameworks.
